title: KV lookup economics: policy constructor and collision-aware key normalizer with safe rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a policy constructor and collision-aware key normalizer to produce safe, cost-aware KV/prefix caching recommendations and a deterministic staged rollout path. This ticket covers modeling lookup economics, producing per-prefix TTL suggestions, transforming observed keys into normalized cache keys (prefix canonicalization + controlled suffixing), and defining automated safety gates for apply/rollback. The output is a small, opinionated policy DSL and a canary orchestrator that uses shadow traffic and a risk budget evaluator.

Why this is needed: existing TTL tuning and keying heuristics are manual and brittle. Customers see oscillating tail costs when teams introduce ad-hoc prefixers or non-deterministic keys (session IDs, ephemeral tokens). We need an automated, explainable way to recommend cache key shapes and TTL ladders while ensuring we can rollback safely without customer impact or latency regression.
acceptance_criteria: A policy constructor service accepts a JSON workload profile and returns per-prefix TTL suggestions and a normalized key template with rationale strings
Key normalizer implements collision detection and emits canonicalized_key plus suffix fingerprint when necessary
A shadow-canary orchestration mode runs for a configurable window and reports: delta miss-rate, token-cost savings estimate, 95th p99 latency delta, and synthetic error rate projection
Safety gates prevent applying a policy if projected request-level cost reduction is < 1% or projected p95 latency worsens > 5ms per-route
Rollback automation can revert to previous policy and run a post-rollback verification that miss-rate and tail latency return to baseline within 30 minutes
implementation_notes: Model: use histogram-based hit-rate estimator per-prefix with exponential decay to prioritize recent traffic
Economics engine: simulate per-token cost under baseline vs candidate policy using measured token distribution and batching impact factors
Key normalization: ruleset to strip high-entropy suffixes, keep canonical prefix shards, add short fingerprint (8-bit) when necessary to avoid collisions
Telemetry: augment existing tracing to tag requests with candidate_normalized_key when in shadow mode
Storage: policy definitions stored in configstore with versioned manifests and immutable revision IDs
rollout_plan: Draft policy in dry-run mode for 24h on 10% shadow traffic
Run economics simulation and compare with dry-run telemetry; compute risk budget consumption
If metrics meet gates, promote to 30% shadow for 48h with active canary checks
If still good, stage 5% live apply increments with 1h observation windows and automatic rollback on gate breach
Fully apply after 7 days of stable metric windows or earlier if cost savings exceed threshold and no regressions
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization rules including edge cases: variable-length IDs, embedded timestamps, UUIDs
Synthetic load tests: inject bursty prefix distributions to validate miss-rate and cache load behavior
Integration: run shadow canary on pre-prod traffic mirror and validate telemetry propagation
Chaos: simulate node OOM and eviction to ensure rollback does not amplify failures
metrics: route-level p95 and p99 latency delta
collision rate for normalized keys (should be < 0.01%)
